target_customer: Homebuilders, electricians and homeowners who buy light switches; builders are the main volume channel
problem: Smart lighting was expensive, needed professional installation and could not be upgraded without turning off power and rewiring.
business_model: Hardware sales of modular switches and backplates through builders, electricians and direct to consumers

founders.name: Derek Richardson
founders.background_notes: The YC page and the Series B release name him as the only founder. Background not found in sources opened. A GeekWire photo caption seen in a search snippet names Alexander Strunkin as another co-founder, but I could not open it (403), so he is not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mains-voltage hardware product with a modular backplate, connected control and a mobile app needed electrical safety certification and hardware iteration, but used standard components.

defensibility.rationale: The modular backplate gives some lock-in once installed and builder relationships help, but connected switches from larger lighting and electrical firms could be matched.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; Deako stayed independent for a decade and agreed to merge with SKYX Platforms in September 2026, closing in October 2026.

market_need_then: Smart home adoption was growing in 2016 but professional lighting control was costly; Deako's own materials say competing whole-home systems cost roughly 200 to 400 dollars per switch (self reported, current).

identity.visual_style: Clean design-forward product marketing with designer faceplates
identity.voice_and_tone: Accessible and builder friendly, premium feel at lower cost

branding.brand_signature: The modular light switch (first and only modular switch, per its site)
branding.community_and_virality: Awards and trade press recognition cited on the YC page; no sources found for fan communities or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press and awards and a Home Assistant integration show niche recognition, but no source shows the name itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Deako stayed independent for about ten years, raising a string of small rounds from 2016 to 2024 and a 12.5 million dollar Series B in 2021 while selling through homebuilders, a channel that gave it volume. Growth did not produce a large independent exit, and it agreed in September 2026 to merge with SKYX Platforms, closing in October 2026 for 25 million SKYX shares per one report.
notes: Directory status says Active but the merger with SKYX closed 2026-10-14 per a press summary, so exit type is merger. Round labels other where sources do not state a stage; the July 2016 round is called the third financing round by the company, the June 2016 1.8M figure comes from a search summary of GeekWire (page returned 403) and may overlap with the July round. Total funding reports conflict (36M in 2021 release, 41.9M CB Insights, 47.2M ZoomInfo, 49.7M GeekWire 2022). No dated competitor source near the batch was found; Lutron Caseta and Brilliant appear only in current sources, so the list is left empty.
